title: Cognitive and Tactile Factors Affecting Human Haptic Performance in Later Life
authors: Kalisch T, Kattenstroth J-C, Kowalewski R, Tegenthoff M, Dinse HR, 2012
research_question: To what extent is the age-related decrease in haptic performance related to the age-related loss of tactile acuity or cognitive capacity?

participants.description: 81 right-handed volunteers (32 males, mean age 67.69±11.22 years; 49 females, mean age 67.06±10.58 years) aged 45 to 94 years. Educational level was balanced. All subjects were neurologically healthy, lucid, independent in daily living, without motor handicaps, and no medication with central nervous effects in the past 5 years. Mini Mental State Examination score > 28.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Custom-made unfamiliar objects from LEGOTM bricks, each a cuboid (1.5 x 2.7 x 4.7 cm) with a specific number and position of rectangular structures (1.6 x 0.8 x 1 cm) on the sides, highlighted by color. Objects had smooth sides, a plain bottom, and a nubby upper side for tactile orientation cues. Total of 17 objects across 5 different sets.
stimuli_or_exposures.source: Figure 5, Methods section 'Cross-modal haptic object recognition test'

measures.instrument: Custom-made cross-modal object recognition test (number of errors)
Apparatus-based two-point discrimination test (2pd-threshold in mm)
Raven Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM) test (percent correct answers)

mechanisms: Haptic object recognition is a demanding task in old age, especially for complex, unfamiliar objects.
Cognition has a disproportionately higher impact on haptic performance compared to tactile acuity.
Increased co-variation between individual sensory performance and general cognitive functioning in old age.

Haptic object exploration involves two phases: a global understanding phase (general exploratory procedure) and a specific detail exploration phase (specific exploratory procedure). Tactile acuity is a predictor only if the first cognitive phase is completed successfully.
Gender differences in haptic performance might be related to visuospatial tasks, mental rotation, and object manipulation experience (males typically more exposed to manual tasks).
The small details (centimeter-range) of the objects require basic tactile acuity.
Aging is associated with greater correlations between intellectual status and sensorimotor performance.
implementation_implications: The findings suggest that interventions targeting cognitive functioning might be more effective than those targeting tactile acuity for improving haptic performance in older adults, especially for complex tasks.
limitations: The use of arbitrary instead of familiar objects might have influenced gender differences in haptic identification, as familiar objects might be heavily overlearned.
The objects used were larger than those in some other studies, which might affect the contribution of proprioceptive functions.

The influences of healthy aging on haptic performance are hard to reveal as they may vary depending on the experimental set-up (pure haptic or cross-modal testing), the objects used (common or unfamiliar, cubic or natural shape), and other boundary conditions (same/different or matching task; time constraints).

environmental_features: common everyday objects (e.g., comb, key, spoon, toothbrush, coin, paperclip, eraser, button, marble, thimble)
stimulus_description.duration_exposure: until object identification or 60-second time limit per object

mechanism_chain.description: Age-related cognitive decline, specifically in working memory and processing speed, mediates the decline in haptic object recognition performance.

instruments_used.name: Haptic Object Recognition Task
instruments_used.description: Participants identified common objects by touch only, without visual input. Measures included number of errors and time to recognition.

instruments_used.name: Digit Span Test
instruments_used.description: Standard neuropsychological test measuring verbal working memory (forward and backward digit span).

instruments_used.name: Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT)
instruments_used.description: Standard neuropsychological test measuring processing speed and attention.
